---
title: "For agents"
subtitle: "A closed vocabulary, a JSON Schema, and errors written to be recovered from"
---

prism is built to be driven by a language model. The agent does the part models
are good at — reading prose and deciding what shape the idea has — and prism
does the part models are bad at: geometry, spacing, alignment and colour.

prism itself never calls a model. It is deterministic: the same spec always
produces byte-identical SVG.

## The envelope

Every spec is a YAML mapping whose top-level `type` selects an archetype.

```yaml
type: flow                   # required — one of the ten archetypes
theme: default               # bundled name, or a path to your own YAML
title: "Ingestion pipeline"  # optional
subtitle: "as of Q3"         # optional
caption: "Source: review"    # optional
width: 900                   # layout hint in px; height follows the content
tokens:                      # optional per-spec theme overrides, dotted paths
  palette.ink: "#0b1020"
```

Everything else in the mapping is the archetype's own payload.

## The shared node

Every archetype consumes the same node shape. This is the vocabulary worth
memorising, because it is the same in all ten:

```yaml
id: ingest                 # optional; needed only when something references it
label: "Ingest"            # required
sublabel: "S3 + Kafka"     # optional
icon: database             # optional; a Lucide icon name
accent: 2                  # optional; ramp index 0-5, or a palette token name
emphasis: normal           # strong | normal | muted
```

Two fields are accepted but **not yet drawn**: `badge` and `note` validate and
then change nothing about the output. They appear in `prism schema` because the
model declares them; ignore them until this page says otherwise, and put the
text in `sublabel` instead.

## Getting the schema

```bash
prism schema flow
```

emits JSON Schema for the archetype's payload, suitable for structured output
or a tool definition. Every archetype rejects unknown fields, so a typo fails
loudly at validation rather than silently rendering the wrong picture.

## Icons

prism vendors all 1756 [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) icons. That is far too many
for a model to choose from reliably, so use this shortlist and reach for
`prism icons` only when nothing here fits:

`activity` `triangle-alert` `archive` `bell` `book` `box` `brain` `briefcase`
`building` `calendar` `chart-line` `check` `circle-check` `clock` `cloud`
`code` `cog` `compass` `cpu` `credit-card` `database` `eye` `file-text`
`funnel` `flag` `flask-conical` `folder` `gauge` `git-branch` `globe` `hammer`
`heart` `key-round` `layers` `lightbulb` `link` `lock` `mail` `map-pin`
`message-circle` `package` `pencil` `phone` `chart-pie` `play` `plug` `rocket`
`search` `send` `server` `settings` `shield` `shield-check` `shopping-cart`
`sparkles` `sprout` `star` `target` `terminal` `trending-up` `truck` `upload`
`users` `wallet` `wrench` `zap`

An unknown icon name fails with a suggestion rather than rendering a blank.

## Errors are part of the interface

prism's exceptions are written for a recovery loop, not for a stack trace. Each
one names the offending value and points at the valid neighbours:

```
unknown icon 'databse' — did you mean: database, data-flow?
unknown archetype 'flowchart' — did you mean: flow?
unknown token 'palette.inc' — did you mean: palette.ink, palette.line?
cell references unknown row 'emae'; known rows: ['emea', 'amer', 'apac']
era 'Pre-revenue' spans unknown event id(s) ['sed']; known ids: ['seed', 'beta']
```

An agent's ability to fix its own output is bounded by the quality of the error
string, so this is treated as a feature surface rather than as diagnostics.

## Choosing an archetype

The decision is about the *shape of the meaning*, not the subject matter:

| If the content is… | Use |
|---|---|
| ordered steps, a process, a pipeline | `flow` |
| containment or reporting structure | `hierarchy` |
| a process that returns to its start | `cycle` |
| events in time | `timeline` |
| two or more options weighed against each other | `comparison` |
| items placed against two independent dimensions | `quadrant` |
| layers of magnitude, or stages that shed volume | `pyramid` |
| tiers of a system, bottom to top | `stack` |
| one centre with several dependents | `hub` |
| values at the intersection of two lists | `matrix` |

When two fit, prefer the one with fewer nodes on screen.
